decision: Which approach best resolves: WF-094 must publish a quote to a public URL, freeze its totals, and share it by link, PDF or email. Which state model should the quote publish workflow implement?

state.problem: WF-094 must publish a quote to a public URL, freeze its totals, and share it by link, PDF or email. Which state model should the quote publish workflow implement?

candidate_solutions.single_status_field: One quote record with a status field. Publishing sets status=PUBLISHED, hs_locked=true, and computes hs_quote_link, hs_domain, hs_slug, hs_quote_number, hs_quote_amount. Unlocking sets status back to DRAFT, PENDING_APPROVAL or REJECTED and clears the computed link. The researched platform models exactly this: publish is a PATCH on hs_status, and the derived properties are read-only computed fields.
candidate_solutions.separate_publication_record: Keep the quote record immutable and write a separate publication record that holds the link, the frozen total and the unlock state. The quote itself never changes.
candidate_solutions.separate_lifecycle_record: Keep the quote immutable and write a lifecycle record per state transition, so publish and unlock are two more rows in a history collection.

research_evidence: hs_quote_link is a read-only property and cannot be set through the API after publishing
hs_domain and hs_slug are set by state
hs_locked is set to true; to modify any properties after publishing you must first update hs_status back to DRAFT, PENDING_APPROVAL or REJECTED
The active quote state has the same price as the draft state, however the overall amount is locked and cannot be modified after it is published
When you click Share the quote moves to a Shared status, even if it has not been sent to the buyer
measured_facts: backend/dsr has 58 existing domain packages and none of them is a quoting package

the seven extendable packages named in the ticket brief are crm_integration, throttle, lead_score, visitor_identification, lead_qualification, round_robin and concierge_router, and none of them is about quoting
records.data is arbitrary JSON, so no option needs a migration
every option can keep every write inside AuditedDatabase
context.cost_of_wrong_answer: A model that stores the link on a separate record contradicts the researched statement that hs_quote_link lives on the quote object, and it cannot answer the question a reader asks, which is what is the public URL for this quote. A model with a transition history adds a collection no consumer of this workflow reads.

decision: Which approach best resolves: WF-094 publishes a quote and freezes its total. It also has a separate SHARED status, which makes the quote publicly viewable without freezing the figures. How should the SHARED to PUBLISHED transition be modelled?

state.problem: WF-094 publishes a quote and freezes its total. It also has a separate SHARED status, which makes the quote publicly viewable without freezing the figures. How should the SHARED to PUBLISHED transition be modelled?

candidate_solutions.shared_may_publish: Allow SHARED to move to PUBLISHED. The freeze is added at that point. Publishing is a second step after sharing, so a seller may hand out a readable link first and commit the figures later. PUBLISHABLE_FROM gains SHARED.
candidate_solutions.shared_is_terminal: Refuse it. SHARED is a fixed state and the totals stay editable until the quote is unlocked to DRAFT and published again from there. PUBLISHABLE_FROM stays the three unlock targets only.
candidate_solutions.publish_replaces_share: Drop SHARED entirely. One publish action that both freezes and makes the quote viewable, and no separate share status.

research_evidence: When you click Share, the quote moves to a Shared status, even if it hasn't been sent to the buyer.
The active quote state has the same price as the draft state. However, the overall amount is locked and can't be modified after it's published.
hs_locked is set to true. To modify any properties after you've published a quote, you must first update the hs_status of the quote back to DRAFT, PENDING_APPROVAL, or REJECTED.
Clicking Share moves the quote to Shared status only if no approval is needed.
In the Copy link, download PDF tab click Copy link or Download PDF.
measured_facts: The research never names SHARED as an unlock target, only DRAFT, PENDING_APPROVAL and REJECTED.
The research never enumerates which statuses are publishable sources, so that set is already a recorded design decision in vocabulary.py.
The product promise is an audit log that describes work that actually happened, so a transition that is refused must be refused loudly rather than silently.
This feature ships a page. A state a seller can reach but never leave is a dead end a reviewer would notice.
context.cost_of_wrong_answer: If SHARED cannot publish, a seller who shared a quote must unlock it all the way back to DRAFT and republish, which discards the shared state and issues a new activity entry. If SHARED can publish, the state machine has one more edge to test and one more meaning for the freeze.

decision: Implementation of WF-094 meets the release bar

state.change_summary: A feature plugin that publishes a quote to a hosted public link, freezes its total, and shares it by link, PDF or email. It adds a domain package backend/dsr/quote_publishing (vocabulary, rules, engine), a feature router on prefix /api/WF-094 with 11 routes, two backend test files with 81 tests, and a frontend feature folder with a page, an api wrapper, local primitives and 19 tests. Publishing is a state transition on the quote record: it sets status, hs_locked, and computes hs_domain, hs_slug, hs_quote_link, hs_pdf_download_link, hs_quote_number, hs_quote_amount, hs_language, hs_locale and hs_timezone. No caller can supply a link, a slug or a domain; a body carrying one is refused with 422. Unlocking moves hs_status back to DRAFT, PENDING_APPROVAL or REJECTED, the only three targets the research names. Sharing is separate from publishing and does not freeze the total. Every write names its serving route in the audit row.

declared_unverified: No browser screenshot was taken. Visual verification in a real browser was not performed in this run.
No screen reader was run against the page. The ARIA roles and live regions are asserted in tests but were not heard.
The coverage figure of 95 percent was measured with four agents running on eight cores. A number measured under contention understates the truth. CI is the authority.
The whole-suite run of 16063 tests was measured locally under the same contention. CI is the authority.
The feature was not reviewed by the reviewer-bot sub-agent in this run.
The Dynamics half of the researched workflow has no public API, so nothing was built for it and no endpoint was invented.
No mail was transmitted. This product has no mail transport, so the workflow records a send event rather than sending. That is a deliberate scope decision, not a stub left unfinished.
state.requirements: A feature adds files and edits no shared file. All reads and writes go through dsr.deps / RecordStore / AuditedDatabase so every mutation writes its audit row in the same transaction. Payloads stay schema-flexible JSON: no migration, no typed column, the envelope untouched. The feature owns a unique route prefix with no colliding concrete (method, path) pair. Tests exist and the whole suite is green. The frontend page builds, is discovered by the glob, and meets the design floor.

verdict.instructions: Should this change land on main? Weigh the balance of the questions above rather than deciding on your own: where contract_compliance, audit_integrity and design_floor are all healthy and the evidence questions show broad coverage, answer merge with the confidence that warrants. Items listed as unverified are declared context to weigh, not defects in themselves -- but a change whose coverage is genuinely thin, or which was recovered from a base far behind main and not reconciled, is fix.
